description.purpose: Turns a topology snapshot into the objects a display holds: one per cell, one per edge, one frame per hive, plus the root that carries the browser half of canvy.
description.use_when: Inside a canvy hive. It is the only cell that patches the display, and it does so on a timer -- a page load costs it nothing at all.
description.not_in_scope: It owns no topology (that arrives by message on this hive's own lane to the colony's read-only graph endpoint) and no position (a cell the display already knows keeps the coordinates it has, because somebody may have dragged it there and a drag never leaves the display). It computes no edge PATH: the orthogonal routing lives in the browser because it is presentation, and one algorithm in two languages is the duplication that avoids. It knows nothing about HTTP, sockets or LiveView.
examples: pass 1: a snapshot -> one read of what the display already holds, the graph riding along on the hop
pass 2: the display's answer -> one bundle of object calls, or the whole bootstrap when the display is empty
pass 3: the display's acknowledgement -> nothing, which is what stops the loop
